newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to strengthen passenger alliances.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to strengthen passenger alliances.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG is to strengthen its passenger alliance network, the carrier's marketing chief executive, Hemjoe Klein, said.

He told the annual conference of the German travel agents association DRV in Orlando, Florida Lufthansa wants a worldwide "seamless travel" system with partners United Airlines and Thai Airways International,
In a speech released here he said this will include integrated timetables, short waiting times, no changes between terminals and a single boarding card or electronic ticket
"Competition between airlines will be replaced by competition between alliance systems. Airlines will secure their position regionally with local (partner) competence," he added.

Klein said Lufthansa's franchise system of feeder services operated by regional airlines such as Augsburg Airways and Contact Air would be extended in Germany and abroad adding that this network was two years ahead of other global alliances in terms of service and standards.
Lufthansa also has strategic agreements with Scandinavian Airlines System, South African Airways and Varig.

Klein said Kufthansa will unveil its new travel agents commissions system on November 15 as part of general cost-saving measures designed to reduce distribution unit costs by 20 percent in the next five years.

Lufthansa generated 50 percent of its revenue but 75 percent of costs in Germany and so had to continue its cost-cutting measures and the recent pay deal with unions for a 1.7 percent salary rise from April 1, 1998, was one element of this, Klein stated.

Travel agents would still experience absolute growth over the next 10 years even if electronic media captured as much as 20-30 percent of sales distribution but Klein said it was a fundamental mistake for agents to give corporate clients large discounts. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
